name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP off-site power lost and restored 8 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov for the 27th time in the war; the IAEA said it was restored hours later
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its off-site electricity on 8 Nov when the Ferosplavna line disconnected, the plant's 27th loss of power since the war began, and the IAEA said supply was restored hours later (Reuters via ThePrint). The IAEA said the cause and location of the fault were unknown; the Russian-installed management cited automatic protection and normal radiation levels. No damage to safety systems or radiological release was reported as of 11 Nov.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the UK from these power losses. Official updates come from the IAEA; for any travel near the region, follow FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Plant lost all off-site power on 8 Nov: Watch line; no safety-system damage or INES 2+ event

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
